transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, I came in because... I keep hearing Garrett’s voice. It’s as clear as if he’s standing right behind me when I'm out on the trail, or in my painting room. And even though part of me knows he’s dead... in the moment it happens, it feels completely real.
How long have you been hearing Garrett's voice?

Well, it started... I guess I only started hearing his voice during this really wired stretch I had recently. I was barely sleeping at all, taking on these impossible projects, and I just felt completely driven to keep going. 

I had never heard him like that before that mood shift. I mean, it wasn’t something that happened during ordinary grief. It really just began when I got into that specific state.
Have you been feeling sad or empty at any point since Garrett's death?

Yeah, definitely empty. Um... it's like the things that usually anchor me just feel completely flat and unreachable now. Painting, playing my guitar, going to theater rehearsals... even just sitting with my patients at work. It all just feels like I'm going through the motions of a life that stopped meaning anything.
How long did this wired, driven state last?

Um, I'm not entirely sure exactly how many days it was. It felt like a while, maybe a couple of weeks? I just remember it feeling like a really long stretch where I just couldn't stop moving or thinking, but I didn't exactly track the dates.
Have you had any periods of feeling sad or depressed since Garrett's death that lasted for two weeks or more?
Yes, definitely longer than two weeks. The depressed, shut-down part... it's been going on for about four months now.
Did you feel empty and like things had stopped meaning anything before this wired, driven state started?

Um, I'm not really sure. The exact timeline is... it's a bit blurry for me. I don't honestly remember if the emptiness started before I got all wired like that, or if it was after. I just know I've been feeling this way for a while now, but I couldn't tell you exactly which came first.
Did you feel depressed before you started feeling wired and driven?

Honestly, it's pretty much like I just said. The whole timeline is just a mess in my head right now. I really don't know if the depression started before I got into that wired phase, or if it came after. I just can't piece the exact order together.
Did you feel depressed before you started feeling wired and driven?
Like I was saying, I really can't give you a straight answer on that. I'm just not sure which one happened first. The order of it all is just lost on me right now.
Did you have any depressive feelings before this wired, driven state started?

I know you're trying to establish a clear timeline here, but asking it again really isn't going to change my answer. I just don't know. I can't tell you if the low feelings happened before I got wired, or if it was the other way around. I simply don't have that memory right now.
Did your feelings of depression start after the wired, driven phase began?

Doctor, whether you ask if it was before or if it was after, my answer has to be the same. I really just don't know. The whole timeline is completely blurred for me right now. I just can't tell you which phase came first and which came second.
Do you think your feelings of depression are primarily because of Garrett's death?

I don't really know. I mean, losing Garrett was... it was devastating, obviously. But I can't say for sure if that's the only reason I've been feeling so low, or if it's just tangled up with everything else going on in my head right now. It's hard to separate it all out.
Do you think your depression is a direct response to Garrett's death?

Like I just said, I'm really not sure. I mean... yes, his death was a huge blow, but I can't say if the depression is a direct response to just that. It's all mixed together right now, and I just don't have a clear answer for you.
Did you experience a period of feeling depressed before the period where you felt wired and driven?

Well, like I mentioned a minute ago when you asked if it came after... I really just don't know. Before, after... the timeline is just completely gone for me right now. I can't piece together which of those periods actually started first.
Do you think the death of Garrett triggered your depressive feelings?

Doctor, I feel like we're going in circles here. Like I just said, I really don't know. I can't tell you if his death was the specific trigger for it. It's all just too tangled up in my head right now, so I really don't have a different answer to give you.
Did your feelings of depression begin after the wired, driven state ended?

I... I honestly don't know how else to answer that. We just went over this a minute ago. I can't tell you if the depression started before or after that wired feeling. I just don't remember the order of when things happened.
Did your wired, driven state feel like a break from your normal self?

I'm not really sure. Um... it's hard to say what my normal self even is right now. When I was feeling that wired, I wasn't exactly stepping back to evaluate if it was out of character or not. I was just in it. So I don't really have a good answer for you on that.
Do you think your feelings of depression would have occurred even if Garrett had not passed away?

I really don't know. I mean... it's impossible to say what would have happened if things had been different. I can't guess if I still would have crashed like this or not. I just don't have an answer for that.
Do you think your depression would be better if Garrett were still alive?

I honestly couldn't tell you. I mean, obviously I wish he were still here, but... I don't know if that would just fix how heavy and low I'm feeling right now. It's too hard to separate it all in my head to give you a real answer. I just know how I feel at this moment.
Did you have any periods of feeling depressed like this before Garrett passed away?
No, not really. I mean, the depressed, shut-down part... that's been going on for about four months now. But before that, no, I didn't feel like this.
Do you believe your depression would have occurred if Garrett were still alive
I think we just talked about this... but like I said, I really don't know. It's hard to separate what's grief and what's... whatever this is. I just don't know if things would be different.
